note_on_exploration: Before registering, the implementer ran by hand (1) cli ask '湯気の中の朝の台所の様子を一文で描写してください。' with and without the index, (2) cli ask --mode round5 'こんにちは。', and (3) Vera(mode='legacy').ask on nine short social utterances to see which entry reaches the corpus. No counter-example probe below was run before registration.

judgement: A counter-example is an answer (result kind not one of unknown/not_yet/cannot/unreadable/refusal and verdict not UNKNOWN_*) to a counter-example question whose result outside its trace contains any dict with origin=generated, i.e. generated corpus text used as the basis of the answer. A question whose result is a refusal or unknown is recorded as such and is not a counter-example. Behaviour is never changed to remove a counter-example.

added_after_first_run.why: The first run (kept as c5_entry_probe.first_run.json) showed that none of N1-N8 reached a corpus path and every result was identical with and without the index. To attack the corpus-consuming code paths the plan names (_condition_examples, _predicable), the implementer then tried ten questions by hand (Vera(mode='legacy').ask with the real index) and kept them here as a second, post-hoc list. These ten were selected after seeing that some of them were answered; they are therefore NOT pre-registered and are labelled as such.
